Performance evaluation of the corrugated (fluting) medium paper machine for integrating the RF and US-Second scenario The dryer section represents the costliest operation in paper production in terms of operating costs due to the high steam requirements. Therefore, the annual operating cost is subject to drying energy costs. Most of the energy consumed in the dryer section is the latent heat used to evaporate water, which represents about 75%. The energy (steam) cost was taken in the range of 75-85% of operating costs [Miller et al., 2005; Lang, I., (2009)]. This percentage may change depending on whether other key contributors to operating costs, such as raw materials, labor, and maintenance, are included or excluded. The reduction in the operating cost associated with a decrease in energy consumption was estimated, as illustrated in Table 12. The decrease in operating costs associated with the reduction in energy costs was considered by excluding maintenance and labor costs. The two scenarios of corrugated medium show a greater reduction percentage in operating cost compared to the two scenarios of the linerboard due to the high energy reduction performance for the two corrugated medium scenarios using RF and US.
